symptom: Kurucz 2005 showed near-zero line depth where the 1984 atlas and the telluric-free IAG atlas agree on deep lines (Al I 6696: 0.008 vs 0.254/0.257; K I 7699: 0.039 vs 0.808/0.807)
expected_behavior: Line depths compared at a common wavelength medium
actual_behavior: irradthu.dat was read as air (scale=10.0, no conversion), displacing every Kurucz line by the air-vacuum offset (~1.7 A at 6600 A, about 200 sampled pixels), so the tight line window sampled continuum instead of the line
root_cause: The Kurucz header states only 'nm' and never states the medium; RYA-929 read it as air without measuring, and flagged the resulting mismatch as a Kurucz product defect
detected_by: RYA-938 cross-correlation registration test against the 1984 air grid
science_impact: No abundance affected - RYA-929 was explicitly diagnostic and blocked Kurucz line substitution. The window-level GO survives: a 1.7 A shift barely moves a 17-300 A window statistic, which is why the defect showed only at line scale
notes_provenance: Measured lag +1.700 A vs predicted air-vacuum offset +1.697 A (3 mA); IAG positive control returns -0.000 A; after vac_to_air all three windows return -0.000 A and Al I 6696 recovers to 0.248 vs IAG 0.257

symptom: A successful molecfit run reported as a failure, with the self-contradicting message 'molecfit_model failed (rc=0)'.
expected_behavior: Product names are a property of the recipe invocation and identical on every machine.
actual_behavior: esorex took --suppress-prefix from ~/.esorex/esorex.rc. The Mac has no rc at all; a fresh ESO source-kit install writes suppress-prefix=FALSE. Under FALSE all ten products are still written, as out_0000..out_0009.fits, so BEST_FIT_MODEL.fits was simply absent.
root_cause: The runner relied on machine-local esorex configuration instead of passing --suppress-prefix=TRUE explicitly.
science_impact: None. A silent-wrong CLASS though: the failure looked like a fit problem and sent the session hunting one that did not exist. The error message now distinguishes a failed recipe from a missing expected product and lists what was produced.
notes_provenance: Found only because a SECOND machine was tried; a single-machine project never sees this class.

symptom: The RYA-929 sweep script still read the Kurucz 2005 product as air after RYA-938 established it is vacuum.
expected_behavior: Kurucz 2005 is converted vacuum->air on read, like every other vacuum product in the repo.
actual_behavior: read_ascii_windows(..., scale=10.0) with no conversion, displacing every line ~1.7 A at 6600 A (~200 sampled pixels).
root_cause: RYA-938 characterised the defect and fixed its own reader, but left the RYA-929 script untouched because that ticket was Done.
detected_by: RYA-939, checking the latent defect RYA-938 flagged out of scope
science_impact: No committed abundance affected. But RYA-933/934 (Kurucz 2005 Fe I / Fe II all-engine reruns) were queued against this script and would have inherited the defect - a line-level table that looks plausible and is displaced by ~200 pixels.
notes_provenance: Fixed by adding an explicit vacuum=True flag to the reader rather than a silent conversion, so the medium is declared at every call site.

symptom: Fitted O2 column collapsed to 0.24 of the reference and the LSF railed at its 100-pixel bound.
expected_behavior: A product that ships its own continuum is consumed with that continuum; none is re-fitted.
actual_behavior: molecfit fitted a free degree-3 continuum across a window one-third saturated by the O2 A band; the polynomial followed the band down (mscal median 0.832 against an atlas median of 0.93), so the band was explained by continuum rather than by absorption.
root_cause: Column 2 of the 1984 atlas is a PSEUDO-RESIDUAL FLUX - unity IS the continuum - and FIT_CONTINUUM was left at 1.
affected_artifacts: none - caught in the pilot, before any product
science_impact: None reached a product. Had it, the correction would have under-removed telluric absorption by a factor of ~4 while looking converged. Same shape as the RYA-911 double-continuum defect.

symptom: reduced chi2 1892, residual 43%, fit terminating after 8 iterations having improved chi2 by 0.02%.
expected_behavior: The FTS wavelength scale is authoritative and is not adjusted.
actual_behavior: chip 1 coef 0 pinned at exactly -0.050000 (its bound, quoted to +/-1e-6), imposing a spurious -3.3 A displacement on the model. A wide cross-correlation found it as a sharp peak at -3.316 A, correlation 0.735 against 0.40 at zero lag.
root_cause: FIT_WLC was left free. With solar lines masked, nothing constrains it, and an FTS atlas's wavelength scale is precisely the thing that should never be fitted - RYA-938 verified this one against IAG at -0.000 A.
science_impact: None reached a product. Note the near-miss: an initial cross-correlation scanned only +/-0.1 A and reported 'no shift', which is how a 3.3 A error survived a check. Fixing it took chi2 1892 -> 24.7 and residual 43% -> 5.0%.

symptom: H2O 7160-7340 A failed with a zero-width LSF from every starting point.
expected_behavior: The starting ladder brackets the instrumental LSF wherever it is applied.
actual_behavior: The ladder was a fixed list in PIXELS (max 4.0), while the measured resolving power implies 5.26 px at 7160 A - every start sat below the answer.
root_cause: Resolving power is an instrument property; FWHM in pixels is not, because atlas sampling runs 0.0067-0.0183 A across 2960-13000 A. A pixel ladder is correct only where it was tuned.
science_impact: None. The ladder is now derived from the MEASURED R = 148,000. The band still does not converge - it genuinely cannot constrain the kernel - but it is now a measured null rather than an artefact of a badly chosen start.

symptom: H2O bands reported 'implied_airmass' of 1.9-2.6 against O2's 1.30-1.35, reading as a contradiction.
expected_behavior: A derived value is reported under the name of what it actually is.
actual_behavior: The harness labelled every rel_mol_col an implied airmass. That is only true for a WELL-MIXED gas: for O2 the abundance term is 1 so the column IS an airmass proxy, but for H2O the column is airmass x (PWV / reference PWV).
root_cause: One label applied to two physically different quantities.
affected_artifacts: data/audit/rya940_kp1984_telluric/*/fit_manifest.json (pre-fix runs carry the old key; the findings table reads either)
science_impact: Would have published a false disagreement between O2 and H2O - or, worse, invited someone to 'reconcile' water vapour with airmass. The O2-only agreement is the actual referee and had to stay uncontaminated by H2O columns.

symptom: Neither telluric-corrected Kitt Peak holding could be measured; the Fe I/Fe II reruns had no way to name them.

But RYA-929's corrected Kitt Peak reference had been unmeasurable since it was registered, and an unreachable holding leaves NO trace: it reads to every caller exactly like having no data (RYA-833). The guard's own gap is the finding worth keeping - `audited` holdings are exempt from it.

product_identity: instrument_catalog telluric_basis vs the file the manifest routes
symptom: instrument_catalog.csv marks iag_fts_solar_atlas telluric_basis=corrected, but solar_reference_holdings_rya708.csv routes that instrument to iag_reiners2016/spvis.dat.gz, which is the telluric-RETAINING base atlas. The telluric-free derivative (iag_baker2020/iag_telfree_solaratlas.fits) is not registered under any instrument_id.
expected_behavior: telluric_basis describes the file that is actually routed, so telluric_policy.exclusion() excludes lines inside O2/H2O bands whenever those bands still contain atmosphere.
actual_behavior: basis=corrected makes exclusion() return '' for every wavelength, so NO line inside any O2 or H2O band is excluded from a holding whose bands are saturated with atmosphere. Measured on the routed file: 46.25 pct of O2 A-band 7594-7685 and 51.63 pct of H2O 9280-9600 lie below 0.5, reaching 0.001.
root_cause: Two IAG atlases with OPPOSITE telluric states are held under one instrument_id. Reiners+2016 is the base; Baker+2020 telfree is the correction. The catalog row carries Baker's property and the manifest carries Reiners' path. The KP-vs-IAG table in pipeline/telluric_policy.py quotes IAG at 0.1/0.0 pct below 0.5, which reproduces Baker (0.18/0.00) and not Reiners (46.25/51.63) - so the docstring and the routing describe different files.
detected_by: RYA-944 four-atlas telluric control; the IAG leg contradicted telluric_policy.py's own table by 46 pp, which is what exposed the split
affected_artifacts: any EW/synthesis product measured from iag_fts_solar_atlas inside an O2 or H2O band
science_impact: Telluric absorption measured as solar line depth. Affects any Fe/other-element line drawn from the IAG holding inside 6867-6884, 7594-7685, 8100-8400 or 9280-9600 A. Scope not yet enumerated.

symptom: The committed RYA-1059 digest stores canonical_gf `line_id` values as its cross-reference. canonical_gf was rebuilt (RYA-1053 re-extend, RYA-1054 dedupe) and the ids SHIFTED, so 87 of 131 matched rows in normalized_lines.csv now resolve to a DIFFERENT physical line -- several to a different SPECIES (Fe I 21735.457 -> the row now at that id is Ni I 21993.985; Fe I 21795.195 -> Sc I 22052.250). CI on main was RED on test_chiappino_digest_rya1059::test_reproducible because of exactly this.
expected_behavior: A stored cross-reference to canonical_gf resolves to the same transition for as long as that transition exists, regardless of what else is added to or removed from the table.
actual_behavior: `line_id` is an OPAQUE ROW-INDEX SURROGATE minted as f'gf_{i:06d}' over the sorted row order (migrate_gf_single_source.py:233). It is a position, not an identity, so any rebuild that inserts or removes a row silently repoints every external reference past that point. The extend scripts (rya822/834/1047/1053) append with start=max+1 and are safe on their own; a dedupe or a re-sort is not.
root_cause: An identifier that is not a function of the thing it identifies. Same class as RYA-1033 (a rounded wavelength is not a key): the join key must be derivable from the line's own physics (species + wavelength + EP), or the surrogate must be assigned once and never recomputed.
detected_by: RYA-1069 PR #427 CI on the Sirius runner; the same test is RED on clean main at 3c0f1d8 and e0e57d7, so it predates that branch
affected_artifacts: REGENERATED HERE: the 4 RYA-1059 csv files (only the line_id column moved -- verified byte-identical on all 182 changed lines once the gf_ token is blanked, and summary.json/fe_jhk_delta.csv unchanged). NOT AUDITED, SAME EXPOSURE: ~19 other committed artifacts store gf_ ids -- data/audit/rya1058_elgueta/, data/audit/rya1060_elgueta_fe_gap/, data/literature/igrins_nandakumar_2024/, and 6 data/results/*.json (rya560/564/565/581/585/592). Each belongs to its own ticket; none was touched here.
science_impact: No published abundance moves -- the RYA-1059 digest is DISCOVERY_REFERENCE_ONLY and mutates nothing. The risk is provenance: a reader following a stored id lands on the wrong transition, and for the cross-species cases that is a wrong ELEMENT. The ~19 unaudited artifacts are unquantified.
regression_test: tests/test_chiappino_digest_rya1059.py::test_reproducible now passes; it detects the SYMPTOM (artifact drift) but not the CAUSE -- nothing yet asserts that a stored gf_ id still resolves to its own species+wavelength.
notes_provenance: Regenerating restores reproducibility and CORRECTS 87 wrong cross-references; it does not fix the unstable key. The durable fix is a physics-derived key or a write-once surrogate, plus a guard that resolves every stored id back to its species+wavelength. Filed as a finding, not fixed here: out of scope for the CI unblock.
